title: Derived transposition on a tensor model with one K-flat factor
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module complexes and localization $Q$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], $E$ a K-injective complex [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $A$ any unbounded complex. Use the total tensor, product Hom complex and normalized derived tensor-Hom structure [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] [def-pur-hom-complex] [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Then $Q(A\otimes_R P)$ canonically computes $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP$. For every chain map $f:A\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,E)$, its derived tensor-Hom transpose is represented by $\widetilde f:A\otimes_R P\to E$, $a\otimes p\mapsto f(a)(p)$. These comparisons are natural in $A,P,E$ and agree with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms of representatives; no K-flatness of $A$ or boundedness is required. The order of factors is $A,P$; interchanging homogeneous factors of degrees $n,m$ introduces $(-1)^{nm}$.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom), proof: arbitrary first complex and K-flat second factor; agent refinement fixing the chain transpose on one-sided models.

proof.text:
Fix $P$. By [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent], $A\mapsto Q(A\otimes_R P)$ inverts all quasi-isomorphisms. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](1) gives a functor $T_P:D(R)\to D(R)$ with $T_P(QA)=Q(A\otimes_R P)$, up to its specified factorization isomorphism. On the full subcategory of K-flat complexes with flat terms, the normalized comparisons $c_{F,P}:Q(F\otimes P)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP$ are natural [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. The equivalence $W^{-1}\mathcal P_R\simeq D(R)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], together with [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), extends this isomorphism uniquely to $T_P\cong(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP)$. Denote its component by $c_{A,P}$. Concretely, choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $q:F\to A$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Then
$$c_{A,P}=(Qq\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)\circ c_{F,P}\circ Q(q\otimes1)^{-1}.$$
Both inverted maps are isomorphisms by the cited quasi-isomorphism-preservation result and localization. Uniqueness of the extension proves independence of $q$ and naturality in $A$. For a chain map $b:P\to P'$ between the allowed second factors, naturality in $P$ on K-flat $F$ is part of the normalized comparison; faithfulness of restriction along the same equivalence gives the naturality square for every $A$.

source.place: Tags 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism), 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction); agent comparison with the fixed normalized tensor.

proof.text:
Construct $\widetilde f$ on each summand $A^n\otimes_R P^m$ by the bilinear map $(a,p)\mapsto f^n(a)^m(p)$. This is compatible with restriction, so the sheafification defining the sheaf tensor and then the direct-sum universal property give a sheaf morphism in every total degree [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product; def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The chain-map identity for $f$, with the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex], reads
$$d_E(f(a)(p))=f(d_Aa)(p)+(-1)^n f(a)(d_Pp).$$
This is exactly the total-tensor chain-map identity. Hence these morphisms form $\widetilde f:A\otimes P\to E$, with no additional sign in this order of factors. Each input tensor section is first mapped by the actual sheafification unit and then the actual total-summand inclusion; the formula specifies those generators, rather than asserting that every tensor-sheaf section is a global pure tensor.

source.place: Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose), underlying component calculation with the differentials of Section 0A8X (section-hom-complexes).

proof.text: The factor interchange on homogeneous sections is $s(a\otimes p)=(-1)^{nm}p\otimes a$ for $a\in A^n$, $p\in P^m$, extended by sheafification and direct sums [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product; def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In $s\,d(a\otimes p)$ the coefficients of $p\otimes d_Aa$ and $d_Pp\otimes a$ are respectively $(-1)^{(n+1)m}$ and $(-1)^{n+n(m+1)}=(-1)^{nm}$. In $d\,s(a\otimes p)$ they are $(-1)^{nm+m}$ and $(-1)^{nm}$, respectively. Thus $s$ is a chain map; the reversed interchange is its inverse since $(-1)^{2nm}=1$. This proves the asserted interchange sign, and permits use of right-K-flat quasi-isomorphism preservation on either tensor side below.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), subsequent commutativity display and its sign convention; expanded direct calculation.

proof.text: Let $u:E\to I(E)$ be the fixed functorial K-injective augmentation [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist; def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. Since $E$ and $I(E)$ are K-injective, [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] with first-variable identity gives a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal Hom(P,u)$. The localization factorization of [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation] consequently identifies $Q\mathcal Hom(P,E)$ with $H(QP,QE)$: first apply $Q\mathcal Hom(P,u)$, then the inverse of $H(QP,QE)\cong Q\mathcal Hom(P,I(E))$. Write $h:QA\to H(QP,QE)$ for the image of $Qf$ under this identification. This uses K-injectivity of $E$, not termwise injectivity of $E$; only its chosen replacement is required to have injective terms.

source.place: Tag 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined) and Section 08J7 (section-internal-hom), construction with a chosen K-injective representative.

proof.text:
Let $\tau$ denote inverse closed transposition from $\operatorname{Hom}(QA,H(QP,QE))$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(QA\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP,QE)$. Use the resolution $q:F\to A$ of step 1 and the chain map $\phi=\mathcal Hom(P,u)\circ f\circ q:F\to\mathcal Hom(P,I(E))$. Both $F$ and $P$ are K-flat, so the normalization in [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] applies. Step 2 identifies its uncurried chain map with $u\circ\widetilde f\circ(q\otimes1)$, since both send $x\otimes p$ to $u(f(qx)(p))$. With the fixed inverse localized augmentation of [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation], normalization says
$$\tau(h\circ Qq)\circ c_{F,P}=Q(u)^{-1}\circ Q(u\circ\widetilde f\circ(q\otimes1))=Q(\widetilde f)\circ Q(q\otimes1).$$
Naturality of the given adjunction gives $\tau(h\circ Qq)=\tau(h)\circ(Qq\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)$. Substitute $c_{A,P}\circ Q(q\otimes1)=(Qq\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)\circ c_{F,P}$ from step 1. Cancel the isomorphism $Q(q\otimes1)$ to obtain
$$\tau(h)\circ c_{A,P}=Q(\widetilde f).$$
This is the required representative formula for the fixed normalized derived adjunction; it does not introduce a new adjunction.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), proof; agent extension of the fixed two-K-flat normalization by a resolution and cancellation.

proof.text:
For chain maps $a:A'\to A$, $b:P'\to P$ and $e:E\to E'$ with $P',P$ K-flat with flat terms and $E,E'$ K-injective, put $f'=\mathcal Hom(b,e)\circ f\circ a$. On a homogeneous generator,
$$\widetilde {f'}(x\otimes y)=e(f(a(x))(b(y)))=(e\circ\widetilde f\circ(a\otimes b))(x\otimes y).$$
Thus the two chain maps are equal by the tensor and direct-sum universal properties [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product; def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves; def-pur-hom-complex]. The fixed augmentation is natural [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], the Hom localization factorization is the fixed one [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation], and $c$ is natural by step 1. Localizing this equality and using step 5 proves simultaneous naturality of the transpose formula. No sign appears for $a,b,e$, which have degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose), functoriality; Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), functoriality after localization.

proof.text: For completeness all representative quasi-isomorphisms used in step 6 become invertible on the indicated models. In $A$ this follows directly from [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent]. For a quasi-isomorphism $b:P'\to P$, fix $q:F\to A$ as in step 1. In the square with top $F\otimes P'\xrightarrow{1\otimes b}F\otimes P$ and bottom $A\otimes P'\xrightarrow{1\otimes b}A\otimes P$, both vertical maps $q\otimes1$ are quasi-isomorphisms by that same lemma. The top map is also one: conjugate it by the signed symmetries of step 3 to $b\otimes1_F$, and apply the lemma using K-flatness of $F$. After localization the bottom map is a composite of three isomorphisms. Thus the tensor model inverts $b$ without K-flatness of $A$. Quasi-isomorphisms between the allowed $P$ representatives, and between the K-injective $E$ representatives, induce quasi-isomorphisms on the Hom side by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. The equalities of step 6 therefore remain equalities after solving for any of these inverse isomorphisms. Independence of a chosen $q$ is already part of step 1. None of these arguments truncates $A$ or requires its terms to be flat; the total degrees use direct sums and the Hom degrees use products exactly as defined.

split_report.summary: Expanded the one-K-flat chain transpose into seven steps: localization and comparison, evaluation chain map, Koszul symmetry, fixed K-injective target comparison, two-K-flat normalization and cancellation, naturality, and inversion of representative quasi-isomorphisms. Reused existing tools throughout; no new nodes and no statement change. Added the definition of flat terms to statement dependencies.

Step 1 factors a quasi-isomorphism-inverting functor and its natural comparison through localization; this is a category-theoretic tool.

Steps 4 and 6 use the fixed natural K-injective augmentation for ordinary ringed-site module complexes.
Steps 4 and 7 compare actual Hom representatives under quasi-isomorphisms into K-injective targets, a generic ringed-site tool.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q117-72a16c6eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full. It makes no new nodes, and the statement is byte-identical to side-live; the only stmt_deps change adds def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules for the stated 'flat terms'. The item has no repair note (so it is not a re-split) and is not in the dropped list. No dependency is merged, there is no cycle (closure of 218 nodes), and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. I read Stacks 08J9 and 06YT in the source, and every cited label matches tags/tags. Step 1: the K-flat tensor quasi-iso lemma lets A↦Q(A⊗P) factor through localization (1); the equivalence in the descent node with localization (2)/(3) extends the normalized c_{F,P} uniquely, and c_{A,P}=(Qq⊗1)c_{F,P}Q(q⊗1)^{-1} follows by naturality. Step 2: with d(g)=d_E g−(−1)^n g d_P, f̃ is a chain map with no sign. Step 3: I recomputed the Koszul coefficients ((n+1)m vs nm+m, and nm vs nm) and they agree. Step 4: Hom(P,u) is a quasi-iso by rhom-well-defined with E and I(E) K-injective. Step 5: φ=Hom(P,u)fq meets the normalization of def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model with ψ=u f̃(q⊗1); adjunction naturality and cancelling Q(q⊗1) give τ(h)c_{A,P}=Q(f̃), and I checked the algebra. Step 6: the variances are right. Step 7: this is exactly the 06YT square, with the top map handled by the step-3 symmetry and the K-flatness of F. Small cases checked: A=0 or P=0, degree 0 (classical uncurrying), odd degrees (sign −1), and non-flat or unbounded A. The closest duplicate candidates are not duplicates: lem-sf-coefficient-tensor-curry-normalization requires both factors K-flat, and the flat-evaluation-roof and étale chain-transpose nodes are about other maps. I accept the six declared tool uses as generic ringed-site and categorical black boxes: kflat-resolution, kflat-tensor-quasiiso, localization-UP (a Mathlib leaf), site-derived-tensor-descent, kinjective-resolutions-exist and rhom-well-defined.
